article.title: Why zoos are good

items.sentence_raw: In my view, it is perfectly possible for many species of animals living in zoos or wildlife parks to have a quality of life as high as, or higher than, in the wild.
Animals in good zoos get a varied and high-quality diet with all the supplements required, and any illnesses they might have will be treated.
items.explain: Q17: The question asks why zoo animals may be **healthier** than wild animals. The passage says zoo animals get a *'high-quality diet with all the supplements'* and *'any illnesses they might have will be treated'* — this means they eat well and get medicine. It also says they do not suffer from *'parasites or injuries'* like wild animals do. So the answer is **A**.

items.sentence_raw: Their movement might be somewhat restricted, but they have a safe environment in which to live, and they are spared bullying and social ostracism by others of their kind.
They do not suffer from the threat or stress of predators, or the irritation and pain of parasites or injuries.
items.explain: Q17: The question asks why zoo animals may be **healthier** than wild animals. The passage says zoo animals get a *'high-quality diet with all the supplements'* and *'any illnesses they might have will be treated'* — this means they eat well and get medicine. It also says they do not suffer from *'parasites or injuries'* like wild animals do. So the answer is **A**.

items.sentence_raw: The average captive animal will have a greater life expectancy compared with its wild counterpart, and will not die of drought, of starvation or in the jaws of a predator.
items.explain: Q18: The passage says *'The average captive animal will have a greater life expectancy compared with its wild counterpart'* — **'greater life expectancy'** means it will **live longer**. So the answer is **TRUE**.

items.sentence_raw: A lot of very nasty things happen to truly 'wild' animals that simply don't happen in good zoos, and to view a life that is 'free' as one that is automatically 'good' is, I think, an error.
Furthermore, zoos serve several key purposes.
Firstly, zoos aid conservation.
Colossal numbers of species are becoming extinct across the world, and many more are increasingly threatened and therefore risk extinction.
items.explain: Q14: The question asks about how **quickly** species can die out. The passage says some species collapses have been *'sudden, dramatic and unexpected'* — **'sudden'** and **'unexpected'** mean they happened very fast. So the answer is **B**.

items.sentence_raw: Moreover, some of these collapses have been sudden, dramatic and unexpected, or were simply discovered very late in the day.
items.explain: Q14: The question asks about how **quickly** species can die out. The passage says some species collapses have been *'sudden, dramatic and unexpected'* — **'sudden'** and **'unexpected'** mean they happened very fast. So the answer is **B**.

items.sentence_raw: A species protected in captivity can be bred up to provide a reservoir population against a population crash or extinction in the wild.
A good number of species only exist in captivity, with many of these living in zoos.
items.explain: Q19: The passage says *'A good number of species only exist in captivity'* — **'only exist in captivity'** means they **can no longer be found in the wild**. So the answer is **TRUE**.

items.sentence_raw: Still more only exist in the wild because they have been reintroduced from zoos, or have wild populations that have been boosted by captive bred animals.
items.explain: Q25: The passage says some species *'have been reintroduced from zoos'* — **'reintroduced'** means they were **raised in zoos and then released into the wild**, which matches option **E**. It also says zoos help people *'be more environmentally conscious'* — this means they **increase public awareness of environmental issues**, which matches option **B**. So the answers are **B** and **E**.

items.sentence_raw: Without these efforts there would be fewer species alive today.

Although reintroduction successes are few and far between, the numbers are increasing, and the very fact that species have been saved or reintroduced as a result of captive breeding proves the value of such initiatives.
Zoos also provide education.
Many children and adults, especially those in cities, will never see a wild animal beyond a fox or pigeon.

While it is true that television documentaries are becoming ever more detailed and impressive, and many natural history specimens are on display in museums, there really is nothing to compare with seeing a living creature in the flesh, hearing it, smelling it, watching what it does and having the time to absorb details.
items.explain: Q16: The question asks for **two ways** of learning about animals **other than** visiting zoos. The passage mentions *'television documentaries'* and *'natural history specimens are on display in museums'* — **'specimens'** here means dead animals you can look at. So the answer is **C**.

items.sentence_raw: That alone will bring a greater understanding and perspective to many, and hopefully give them a greater appreciation for wildlife, conservation efforts and how they can contribute.

In addition to this, there is also the education that can take place in zoos through signs, talks and presentations which directly communicate information to visitors about the animals they are seeing and their place in the world.
This was an area where zoos used to be lacking, but they are now increasingly sophisticated in their communication and outreach work.
items.explain: Q21: The question says zoos have **always** been good at giving information. But the passage says *'This was an area where zoos used to be lacking'* — **'used to be lacking'** means they were **not good** in the past. So the answer is **FALSE**.

items.sentence_raw: Many zoos also work directly to educate conservation workers in other countries, or send their animal keepers abroad to contribute their knowledge and skills to those working in zoos and reserves, thereby helping to improve conditions and reintroductions all over the world.
items.explain:
Q23: The passage says zoos *'send their animal keepers abroad to contribute their knowledge'* — this matches option **B** (*'travel to overseas locations'*). It also says they *'educate conservation workers in other countries'* — this matches option **D** (*'teach people involved with conservation'*). So the answers are **B** and **D**.

It also says they *'educate conservation workers in other countries'* — this matches option **D** (*'teach people involved with conservation'*). So the answers are **B** and **D**.

items.sentence_raw: Zoos also play a key role in research.
If we are to save wild species and restore and repair ecosystems we need to know about how key species live, act and react.
Being able to undertake research on animals in zoos where there is less risk and fewer variables means real changes can be effected on wild populations.
items.explain: Q15: The question asks why studying animals in **captivity** is **preferable** to studying them in the wild. The passage says research in zoos has *'less risk and fewer variables'* — **'less risk'** means it is safer, and **'fewer variables'** means it is easier to control. So the answer is **E**.

items.sentence_raw: Finding out about, for example, the oestrus cycle of an animal or its breeding rate helps us manage wild populations.

Procedures such as capturing and moving at-risk or dangerous individuals are bolstered by knowledge gained in zoos about doses for anaesthetics, and by experience in handling and transporting animals.

This can make a real difference to conservation efforts and to the reduction of human-animal conflicts, and can provide a knowledge base for helping with the increasing threats of habitat destruction and other problems.
In conclusion, considering the many ongoing global threats to the environment, it is hard for me to see zoos as anything other than essential to the long-term survival of numerous species.

They are vital not just in terms of protecting animals, but as a means of learning about them to aid those still in the wild, as well as educating and informing the general population about these animals and their world so that they can assist or at least accept the need to be more environmentally conscious.

It also says zoos help people *'be more environmentally conscious'* — this means they **increase public awareness of environmental issues**, which matches option **B**. So the answers are **B** and **E**.

items.sentence_raw: Without them, the world would be, and would increasingly become, a much poorer place.

orphan_explain_map.20: Q20: The passage talks about TV documentaries becoming more detailed, but it never says this caused **increased numbers of zoo visitors**. The passage does not connect these two ideas at all. ***NOT GIVEN is not the same as FALSE*** — so the answer is **NOT GIVEN**.
orphan_explain_map.22: Q22: The passage says research in zoos has *'less risk'* for the researchers, but it never mentions if studying animals in zoos is **less stressful for the animals** themselves. This specific comparison about animal stress is missing. So the answer is **NOT GIVEN**.
